articles.title: "Send opened Outlook instead of sending"
articles.summary: That's the fallback transport: Power Automate is off or has no flow URL.

beginner.text: When Power Automate is disabled (the default) or its flow URL is empty, every Send falls back to opening a pre-filled Outlook window — with formatting stripped and no signature. This is by design, not a failure.

items: Fix: Settings → enable Power Automate and paste your flow URL.
Verify: send a test email — it should go silently with your signature attached.
Bulk warning: with the fallback active, a bulk send opens one Outlook window per recipient.

articles.title: "A variable shows as {{unresolved}}"
articles.summary: The page doesn't contain that data, the page type doesn't match, or a code variable failed.

items: Wrong page type — order variables only resolve on order pages, contact variables on contact pages. Check the template's type matches where you're using it.
Data genuinely missing — if the contact has no phone, {{phone}} stays empty. Use an OR-block ({{phone|email}}) or a conditional block so the sentence drops out cleanly.
Page not finished loading — variables scrape the live page; let it render, then reopen the popup.
Code variable error — open the template in the editor and test the expression; a thrown error resolves to empty.

intermediate.text: The popup highlights unresolved variables before you send — treat any highlight as a stop sign for that email.

articles.title: "The Gift Catalog looks stale or is missing items"
articles.summary: The catalog is a local index that refreshes every 24 hours — force a rebuild or shorten the interval.

beginner.text: The catalog indexes the whole site and caches the result locally for speed. New products or price changes appear after the next re-index — every 24 hours by default.

items: Force it now: use the catalog's rebuild/refresh control and give it a few seconds.
Refresh more often: Developer Settings → 'Gifting Catalog: re-index interval (hours)'. Setting 0 re-indexes on every open (slow first paint).

articles.title: "A modal or button isn't appearing"
articles.summary: Usually a feature toggle, the wrong page type, or an administrator-managed policy setting.

items: Check the feature toggle — Settings → Features. Off means no buttons, no shortcut, no shelf action.
Check the page type — most tools are context-aware: Margin Calc lives on order pages, Call Log on contact/account pages. The shelf only shows actions valid here.
Reload the page — the extension injects on load; a page open since before an update may miss UI.
Right site — tools appear on golfballs.com CRM pages (and the order-notes iframe), nowhere else.

advanced.text: A lock badge means the authenticated server policy manages that visible value; a missing toggle is independently marked hidden. A RevStack administrator can change either state in the global or per-installation policy editor.

articles.title: "Margin calculator shows no cost"
articles.summary: Cost lookups need an active session on the office portal; cached costs can also be stale.

items: Sign in: cost and inventory data come from the office portal (gbcadmin) using your session. Open it in another tab, sign in, retry.
Third-party cookies: lookups run in a first-party context for exactly this reason — if it still fails, reload the order page to restart the fetch frame.
SKU mismatch: costs key on the human SKU (e.g. B3273). Items asterisked in a breakdown couldn't be priced — run a cost sync to fill the gaps.
Stale cache: inventory caches for ~6 hours; a fresh sync forces an update.

articles.title: "Date update failed mid-way"
articles.summary: The save is a multi-step form chain; the step toast names where it stopped — re-open and retry.

intermediate.text: Saving order dates walks a multi-step form sequence on the admin site (load calendar → select approval → select commitment → submit). If a step fails — usually an expired admin session or a slow response — the progress toast names the failing step and the chain stops.

items: Retry: re-open the Order Date Manager and run the update again; the chain restarts from the beginning and is safe to repeat.
Still failing at step one: your admin.icustomize.com session likely expired — reload the order page so the iframe re-authenticates.
Verify: after a success toast, the dates are on the order record; spot-check the first few times.

articles.title: "3D preview is black or blank"
articles.summary: Almost always a graphics-driver quirk — known on Windows-on-ARM machines — not missing artwork.

items: Known hardware case: some Windows-on-ARM machines (Snapdragon GPUs) rendered the logo decal black. Current builds work around it — update the extension first.
GPU acceleration: check chrome://gpu for 'Hardware accelerated' WebGL; reset chrome://settings/system if disabled.
Transient context loss: close the modal and reopen — the 3D context rebuilds.
Diagnostics: Developer Settings → 'Golfball viewer: render diagnostics' prints render info to the console for a bug report.

articles.title: "My settings vanished"
articles.summary: Two suspects: an imported preset overwrote them or the remote administrator policy manages them.

items: Imported a preset recently? Settings scopes overwrite on import. Re-apply your own preset if you saved one — exporting a personal backup preset first is the habit that prevents this.
A specific toggle is gone (not just off)? The server policy hides it — ask a RevStack administrator.
The whole Developer Settings section is gone? The server policy hides that section for non-administrator installations.

advanced.text: Policy changes belong in the RevStack database editor. Global and per-installation management are explicit; the legacy YAML is read only once to seed an empty policy database.
